note: Switch "fleets" (test 5, docs/council/2026-11-27-units-ground-navy.md Part 3, thread 47). Each side has one named fleet counted in squadrons, sound or damaged; one order a season; the crossing; the blockade; the sea threat that holds the army home; one sea-battle scene; the admiral as a rival; who rows. The pattern is from Diodorus 14 (quoted in the council file and in docs/research/big-scenes-history.md); every number here is invention.

orders.name: Watch the crossing
orders.text: Lie in wait for Carthage's transports and convoys at sea.

orders.name: Escort the grain
orders.text: Guard your own grain ships; the fleet brings grain each autumn.

orders.name: Blockade
orders.text: Close the sea to a port your army besieges, so it gets no grain by ship.
orders.source: Motya cut off from the sea, 397 (Diodorus 14.48-49)

orders.name: Carry the army
orders.text: Carry your army from port to port in one season. An enemy fleet watching the lane may bring on a battle at sea first.
orders.source: the army on the shore as the fleet's refuge (Diodorus 14.59.6)

orders.name: Stay in harbour
orders.text: Keep the ships in the Great Harbour and do nothing at sea.

rowers.name: Citizens
rowers.text: Free, but the citizens are armed and bolder: a victory won without you makes them bolder against you.

rowers.name: Hired rowers
rowers.text: One silver a season for every two squadrons. Unpaid, a squadron deserts.
rowers.source: invention, after Republic of Rome's fleet upkeep

rowers.name: Freed slaves
rowers.text: Two more squadrons at once, an emergency measure. The rich families resent losing their slaves.
rowers.source: Diodorus 14.58.1 (the anger of the rich is invention)

plans.label: Close order
plans.note: Keep the line. A loss by 1 becomes a draw.
plans.source: Dionysius ordered Leptines "to engage with his ships in close order, and not to break his line" (Diodorus 14.59.7)

plans.label: Strike ahead
plans.note: +1, but a loss becomes a rout: twice the ships lost.
plans.source: Leptines went ahead "in no cowardly fashion, but without prudence" (Diodorus 14.60.2)

rash.text: {admiral} wants to strike ahead with the best of the ships.
rash.why: he is bold, as Leptines was at Catana in 396

options.label: Let him go
options.note: +1, but a loss becomes a rout.

options.label: Hold him to close order
options.note: A loss by 1 becomes a draw. He may go ahead anyway (1 or 2 on a die).

won.label: Chase them
won.note: 4 or more on a die: one more of their squadrons taken. Less: one of yours is damaged.

won.label: Row home with the prizes
won.note: Take what you won and go.

lost.label: Fight on
lost.note: 5 or more on a die: you save one squadron. Less: you lose one more.

lost.label: Break off and row for home
